Questions: What are the power and drivetrain options for the bZ4X?
Answers: The bZ4X can be equipped with either a single electric motor (front-wheel drive) with 201 horsepower or two electric motors (all-wheel drive) with 215 horsepower. Upgrading to the dual-motor all-wheel drive costs an additional $2080.

Answers: The bZ4X has a slightly larger footprint than the RAV4 but is also slightly lower in height.

Answers: The EPA range estimates for the front-wheel-drive model are 242/252 miles (Limited/XLE), while the all-wheel-drive version is rated at 222/228 miles. In real-world highway testing, the dual-motor model achieved a disappointing 160-mile range.

Questions: How long does it take to charge the bZ4X?
Answers: Using a Level 2 charger, the 6.6-kW onboard charger can replenish the battery in 9 hours. At a DC fast-charger, adding 80% charge takes just under an hour. The front-drive variants peak at 150 kW charging rates, while the dual-motor version maxes out at 100 kW.

Questions: What are some of the standout interior features of the bZ4X?
Answers: The bZ4X features a spacious, airy interior with a digital gauge display and a 12.3-inch central touchscreen. Questions: Does the bZ4X offer one-pedal driving?
Answers: No, the bZ4X does not offer true one-pedal driving. It has two levels of regenerative braking: none and some, with the latter activated via a button on the center console.

Questions: What infotainment and connectivity features are included in the bZ4X?
Answers: All models come standard with a 12.3-inch infotainment touchscreen, wireless Apple CarPlay and Android Auto, a 7.0-inch digital gauge display, cloud-based navigation, an onboard Wi-Fi hotspot, and wireless smartphone charging. The Limited trim offers an optional nine-speaker JBL stereo system.

Questions: Are there any special offers or incentives for bZ4X buyers?
Answers: Toyota includes a year of free charging at EVgo locations with the purchase of a bZ4X.

Questions: How does the bZ4X handle in terms of driving and performance?
Answers: The bZ4X offers perky acceleration and absorbs bumps well without feeling floaty. The steering is reasonably well-weighted, but the performance, especially in the dual-motor version, is not as powerful as some competitors.
